decisions.quote: The returned results included 16 SNPs associated with FPG in the Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium (MAGIC) study [2]. The MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs (ESM Table 2) for a total of 29 SNPs that we attempted to replicate in our African-American cohort.
decisions.location: Methods, Statistical analyses (line 9); References ref. 2 (line 100); ESM Table 2 (lines 117-132)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row (873) and blind target 0 correctly identify the MAGIC meta-analysis by Dupuis et al. (2010), 'New genetic loci implicated in fasting glucose homeostasis and their impact on type 2 diabetes risk' (Nat Genet 42:105-116; ref. [2] and ESM Table 2), as a primary original GWAS whose 16 fasting plasma glucose (FPG) SNPs were re-tested in the HUFS African-American cohort.

decisions.quote: Of the 16 SNPs recently reported in the MAGIC metaanalysis of over 122,000 participants [2], 12 were available for testing in the HUFS dataset (ESM Table 2). We directly replicated three SNPs (rs2191349, rs11558471 and rs4506565) located in or near DGKB-TMEM195, SLC30A8 and TCF7L2 genes respectively (Table 1). We also replicated SNPs from other GWASs for FPG: rs2722425 within ZMAT4 (p value=0.024) as well as rs625643 (p value= 0.048), which is located in a functionally unknown region on chromosome 1 (Table 1). SNPs from the remaining studies that did not directly replicate are not shown.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'mixed'. Of the 12 directly testable MAGIC SNPs from Dupuis et al. (2010), 3 directly replicated (rs2191349 in DGKB-TMEM195, rs11558471 in SLC30A8, and rs4506565 in TCF7L2, p < 0.05 in Table 1) while the remaining 9 did not directly replicate; even including local LD-based replication in Table 2, only 6 MAGIC loci (adding G6PC2, GCKR, and MTNR1B) replicated while the remaining tested MAGIC loci (PROX1, ADCY5, SLC2A2, GLIS3, ADRA2A, CRY2, MADD) did not.

decisions.quote: Here, we conducted replication of published GWAS results for FPG in African-Americans from the metropolitan area of Washington DC, USA.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'replication'. The paper uses genotype and phenotype data from an independent sample of 927 unrelated non-diabetic African-American participants in the Howard University Family Study (HUFS) to re-test previously published GWAS SNP associations with fasting plasma glucose, including those reported by Dupuis et al. (2010).

decisions.location: Methods, Statistical analyses (lines 9-10); Results (lines 16-17); References ref. 5 (line 102); ESM Table 2 (line 133)
decisions.quote:
The MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs (ESM Table 2) for a total of 29 SNPs that we attempted to replicate in our African-American cohort.
Our replication effort occurred in two stages. In the first stage, we attempted to replicate 20 of the 29 exact published SNPs (i.e. direct replication) available in the HUFS dataset. For this stage, SNPs were considered replicated if the same HUFS SNP had a p value <0.05. For the second stage, we performed a local replication analysis based on a 500 kb linkage disequilibrium (LD) block containing a query SNP determined by the SNPs most distant from the query SNP with r 2 ≥0.3. We used the HapMap CEU LD data (http://hapmap.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ downloads/ld_data/2008-06/00README.TXT) for all SNPs except for rs2166706 where the Gujarati Indians in Houston, Texas, USA (GIH) reference dataset (http:// hapmap.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/downloads/ld_data/2008-09_ phaseIII/00README.txt) was used to match the original reported GWAS population [5].
decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests the fasting plasma glucose (FPG) association of SNP rs2166706 near MTNR1B (11q21) reported by Chambers et al. (2009) (ref. [5], Diabetes 58:2703-2708; ESM Table 2 line 133, Excel serial date 40028.0 = 2009-08-04) in 927 unrelated non-diabetic African-American participants from the Howard University Family Study (HUFS). Specifically, rs2166706 was one of the 13 additional SNPs from prior GWASs included in the 29-SNP replication pool, was directly tested in Stage 1 (failing to reach p < 0.05, as Results line 16 reports that SNPs from remaining studies that did not directly replicate are not shown), and was specifically queried in Stage 2 local LD-based replication using the HapMap GIH reference panel to match the original Indian Asian discovery population of ref. [5]. This original study is distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520, which tested MAGIC meta-analysis SNP rs10830963 at MTNR1B) and from sibling target 2 (Bouatia-Naji et al. 2008, Nat Genet, which reported rs1387153 at MTNR1B in European cohorts) as well as targets 3-6. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests the fasting plasma glucose (FPG) association of SNP rs1387153 near MTNR1B (11q21) reported by Bouatia-Naji et al. (ESM Table 2 line 134, PubMed ID 19060909, Nat Genet, Excel serial date 39789.0 = 2008-12-07, giving year 2008) in 927 African-American participants from the HUFS cohort. In Methods (lines 9-10), the authors state that the 16 MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs listed in ESM Table 2 for a total of 29 SNPs attempted for replication via Stage 1 direct replication (rs1387153 had no 'c' exclusion footnote and did not achieve p < 0.05; Results line 16) and Stage 2 500 kb LD-block local replication. This work is an independent GWAS discovery paper distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520, the later MAGIC meta-analysis testing rs10830963 at MTNR1B) and from sibling target 1 (Chambers et al. 2009, Diabetes, testing rs2166706 in Indian Asians and Europeans) as well as targets 3-6. Author and year fields reflect the exact metadata printed in ESM Table 2. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.reason: The source paper empirically re-tests two fasting plasma glucose (FPG) SNP associations reported by Meigs et al. (ESM Table 2 lines 136-137, PubMed ID 17903298, BMC Med Genet, Excel serial date 39344.0 = 2007-09-19, giving year 2007): rs2722425 in ZMAT4 (8p11.21) and rs180730 in PRDM5 (4q27). In the HUFS African-American cohort, rs2722425 was directly replicated in Stage 1 (β = 0.01326, p = 0.024; Results line 16, Table 1 line 47) and locally replicated via three LD proxies in Stage 2 (including rs1823643, corrected p = 0.007; Table 2 lines 93-95), whereas rs180730 did not replicate (Results line 16). Discussion (line 21) explicitly contrasts ZMAT4 with the shipped MAGIC meta-analysis (row 873, Dupuis et al. 2010), noting that ZMAT4 was 'identified in previous GWASs but not replicated in the MAGIC meta-analysis'. Meigs et al. (2007) in BMC Med Genet is also a distinct paper reporting different SNPs and analyses from sibling target 5 (Florez et al. 2007, Diabetes, PubMed ID 17848626, which integrated multi-cohort replication datasets and reported 7 completely different SNPs including rs625643) as well as targets 1-3 and 6. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

(ESM Table 2 lines 138-144, PubMed ID 17848626, Diabetes, Excel serial date 39335.0 = 2007-09-10, giving year 2007), which contributed 7 of the 13 non-MAGIC SNPs in the 29-SNP replication pool (rs625643 in AK024684 on 1p32.3, rs952635 in PDE4B, rs7531174 in SLC44A3, rs1489100 in AJ012503, rs2806739 on 13q21.1, rs2241119 in TSHR, and rs2009833 in ATP8B4). Five of these SNPs were directly tested in Stage 1 (while PDE4B and ATP8B4 were unavailable for direct comparison; Results line 16), with rs625643 directly replicating (β = 0.01141, p = 0.048 in text / 0.05 in Table 1 line 46) and locally replicating via LD proxy rs671431 in Stage 2 (corrected p = 0.04; Table 2 line 82, Discussion line 22), while the remaining tested SNPs did not replicate. Florez et al. (2007) is completely distinct from the sole shipped row (873, Dupuis et al. 2010, Nat Genet 42:105-116, doi:10.1038/ng.520) and is a separate publication reporting a disjoint set of multi-cohort integrated SNPs from sibling target 4 (Meigs et al. 2007, BMC Med Genet, PubMed ID 17903298, which reported rs2722425 in ZMAT4 and rs180730 in PRDM5) as well as targets 1-3 and 6. Prior adjudication covered only row 873 (target 0), and no prior state file existed.

decisions.location: Current Table2, other FPGGWASs; ESMTable2Rungreference and Methods/Discussion, read alongside complete Rungand publisherDupuisoriginals
decisions.reason: The complete current report selects rs2943641from the explicitly identified Rung2009catalogue report, places it under other FPGGWASs with reportedP=.05, and empirically tests its local LDproxies for continuous log-FPG in927new non-diabetic African-Americans. Complete Rungmain/supplement primary tables actually report continuous FPGtests, including DESIRadditiveP=.05, despite the title emphasizingT2Dand its overall prose reporting noFPGassociation. Retesting a published null/boundary test is eligible; neither a positive prior effect nor exact-SNP numerical recovery is required. The current matching benchmark and source attribution establish an empirical locus/trait retest, not only T2Dmechanism discussion. The represented873Dupuisreport supplies the separateMAGICbenchmark; current16MAGIC versus other-GWASselection and RungESMidentity distinguish the targeted reports. Newly inspected Dupuisbody/publisher57-page supplement and two-sheet study-characteristics workbook report IRS1rs4675095FI/HOMA-IR and rs2943641FI/HOMA-IR, not the specific RungDESIRFPGcomparison used here. SharedDESIR/Inter99cohort names do not make those analyses alternate reports of this original trait/model finding. All supplied shipped/corrected identities and sibling loci checked; no extra pair from DOI/year differences alone. ExactNIHMSsupplement3and byte/version equivalence to publisher alternatives remain unverified; no absence claim about every unseen supplementary statistic is made or needed to identify the positively named Rungtest. The proxy/allele-phase differences and originaltable/prose tension preclude an outcome inference here; outcome remains unrequested. Current source prints no originalDOI, so none added from outside metadata.
